summary: This article explains how the old Arabian tradition of camel racing works today, why child jockeys were banned, and how remote-controlled robot jockeys took their place.
introduce: Show the title “Camel Racing and Robot Jockeys” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: a custom or activity passed down from older people to younger people
a person or machine that rides an animal in a race
a machine that can do jobs, often controlled by a computer

challengeTerms.def: traditions, customs, and history passed down through generations
a device used to control a machine from a distance (short for remote control)

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that robots are a good way to keep old sports alive? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain the problem that led to robot jockeys and how robots solved it.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review tradition, jockey, and robot, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses heritage, lightweight, and remote to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
